blocks.content: Deleting an entire StatefulSet follows the same reverse-ordering principle as scaling down, Pods are terminated one at a time, from the highest ordinal down to zero, a controlled, predictable shutdown, not a simultaneous teardown.
1. One Pod at a Time, Not All at Once
blocks.text: 1. One Pod at a Time, Not All at Once

blocks.content: When a StatefulSet is deleted (or scaled down to zero), its Pods do not all terminate simultaneously, they are torn down one at a time, following exactly the same discipline covered in the Ordered Scaling topic.

blocks.alt: A controlled, sequential teardown, not a simultaneous mass termination

blocks.content: 2. Highest Ordinal First, Down to Zero
blocks.text: 2. Highest Ordinal First, Down to Zero

blocks.content: The order is exactly the reverse of creation, the highest-numbered replica terminates first, working backward, with app-0, the very first replica ever created, being the very last one to go.

blocks.alt: The mirror image of creation order, working all the way back down to app-0

blocks.content: 3. Each Fully Terminates Before the Next Begins
blocks.text: 3. Each Fully Terminates Before the Next Begins

blocks.content: This is a genuine, enforced sequence, not just an ordering preference, one Pod must fully finish terminating before the next one's termination even begins, exactly the same discipline applied to creation in the Ordered Deployment topic.

blocks.alt: A real, enforced sequence, one full termination before the next even starts

blocks.content: A Deployment's Pods, being interchangeable, can all terminate at the same time with no coordination needed, a StatefulSet's Pods, given the individual identity and role covered throughout this module, always terminate one at a time instead.

blocks.alt: Simultaneous teardown for interchangeable Pods, strict sequencing for individually identified ones

blocks.content: This ordered, predictable shutdown sequence is genuinely valuable for coordinated, stateful clusters, a database cluster shutting down its replicas one at a time, in a known, consistent order, is meaningfully safer than an abrupt, simultaneous teardown of every node at once.

blocks.alt: A genuinely safer, more controlled shutdown for coordinated, stateful systems

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: StatefulSet termination mirrors ordered scaling, Pods are torn down one at a time, highest ordinal first, each fully terminating before the next begins.
This controlled, predictable shutdown sequence is a real operational benefit for coordinated, stateful clusters, meaningfully safer than an abrupt, simultaneous teardown.
